My family has worked this land in Quzhou for three generations. I know what this soil wants, and I know what the market needs. There is really only one sensible rotation here — winter wheat, then summer maize on the same fields. My neighbors do it, my father did it, and I do it. I have about 12 mu of flat irrigated ground.

For wheat, I already put it in last October. I use improved seed from the county cooperative — varieties like Aikang 58 that the village seed shop sells. I do not trust my own saved seed anymore, yields dropped when I tried. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then urea when the wheat joints in spring. I water four times: the winter water before freeze, jointing, heading, and grain fill. I spray herbicide in early spring when the broadleaves come up, and one more time near heading for aphids or rust if I see it.

After wheat comes off in June I rotate straight into hybrid maize — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has that year. I use the rotary tiller to knock down the stubble, then seed. I put compound fertilizer down at planting and top up with urea at the big bell stage. Maize catches the summer rains mostly, but I run the well twice if July is dry. One herbicide spray after emergence, and I watch for corn borer but often skip spraying if it looks light.

I am 61. I am not going to experiment with new crops. Cotton used to be grown here but the price collapsed. Vegetables need too much labor and my knees are bad. Wheat and maize, every year. Stable price, machines handle most of the heavy work, and I know exactly what to do.
